test_title: PYST 9: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct idiom for the word highlighted in bold.

Ravi found himself in deep water after he ran over a pedestrian while driving under the influence of alcohol near his apartment.

options.text: Ravi was enjoying a swim in a river.
Ravi was learning how to drive.

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Ravi was in serious trouble. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"in deep water"** means being in a difficult or serious situation or trouble. (मुसीबत में होना) • **Example:** After missing multiple deadlines, she found herself in deep water with her boss. • In this context, Ravi is in serious trouble because he caused an accident while driving under the influence of alcohol. (गंभीर परेशानी में होना) • **Example:** Ravi was arrested because he violated the law, putting himself in deep water. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: Ravi was enjoying a swim in a river.** (रवि नदी में तैराकी का आनंद ले रहा था) This is a literal interpretation and does not capture the idiom's meaning. • **Example:** Ravi enjoys swimming in rivers during the summer season. • **Option 3: Ravi was learning how to drive.** (रवि गाड़ी चलाना सीख रहा था) This is unrelated to the context of the sentence and does not apply. • **Example:** Ravi took driving lessons for three months before his test. • **Option 4: Ravi was helping the pedestrian.** (रवि पैदल यात्री की मदद कर रहा था) This is incorrect because the sentence clearly states that Ravi caused the accident. • **Example:** Ravi helped the pedestrian cross the road safely. 32:T98a, The correct answer is: **Arachnophobia**.
